name: OpenComputer

modes.label: On-demand sandbox per second ($0.060 per GB-hour, flat across sizes)
modes.note: docs-v1 reserved-capacity page: 'instant (overage) bills at $0.060/GB-hour ... Both rates are flat across sandbox sizes.' Billed on the memory tier; vCPU follows the tier (1 GB = 1 best-effort vCPU, 4 GB = 1, 8 GB = 2, 16 GB = 4; elasticity.md). Live resize by API; autoscale between tiers is opt-in and off by default. Hibernated time bills no compute. Free-tier orgs are capped at 4 GB.

modes.label: Reserved capacity per 15-min interval ($0.012 per GB-hour, booked ahead)
modes.commit_note: Book memory in 4 GB steps per 15-minute UTC interval, at least 30 min ahead; billed whether used or not; no cancellation or refund. Use above the booking bills at the on-demand $0.060/GB-hour. Priced here only for machines kept on all month.
modes.note: docs-v1 reserved capacity: 'Pre-booked capacity bills at $0.012/GB-hour; instant (overage) bills at $0.060/GB-hour'. Same tiers as on-demand.

modes.label: Machine pool per month (Free, Medium $300, Large $3,000)
modes.commit_note: Homepage tiers: 'Free: shared upto 2vCPU, shared upto 2GB memory, 3GB disk, 5 concurrency'; 'Medium ($300/mo): 8 CPU, 16GB memory, 50GB disk (addable), 50 concurrency'; 'Large ($3,000/mo): 64 CPU, 512GB memory, 3800GB disk, 500 concurrency'; Custom: talk to us. 'Users can add one or more machines to their pool at any time' (price of an added machine not published, so not modeled).
modes.note: Flat monthly pool shared by all sandboxes in it. Per-sandbox size limit inside a pool is not published. Overage, billing period and hibernation billing are not stated on the page.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: No published sandbox subscription: on-demand and reserved bill per GB-hour; pool tiers are priced in the pool mode. Free-tier orgs are capped at 4 GB per sandbox; how an org leaves the free tier is not stated. On-demand concurrency is not published.

extras.item: @Computer coding agent (Slack or API; runs Claude Code and Codex)
extras.price: Trial 3 days / 600 work minutes; Pro $20/mo for 2,000 work minutes; Max $200/mo for 25,000; then $0.01 per minute from prepaid credit packs. Models: your own at no charge, or theirs at API prices.

extras.item: Disk above 20 GB (closed beta, up to 256 GB)
extras.price: Per second 'at a rate comparable to AWS EBS gp3'; dollar rate unpublished
'roughly 2x cheaper than on-demand sandboxes'; exact rate unpublished

features.ip_note: Browser Sessions (managed Chromium over CDP, profiles, live view) are an invite-only preview; sandbox egress goes through OpenComputer's host proxy; no residential/proxy product documented.

perf_source: ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 4.28 s is from an older run (not in the 2026-11-06 run); one-at-a-time start 76 ms (sequential TTI, latest published run 2026-08-07 or older). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results

knobs.label: Share of session wall-time the machine is awake (rest hibernated)
knobs.why: Sandboxes hibernate after an idle timeout and hibernated time bills no compute. Docs disagree on the default (300 s on the overview, 0 = never on the timeout page), so set a timeout to be sure.

caveats: Three ways to pay for sandboxes: on-demand $0.060 per GB-hour, reserved $0.012 per GB-hour (booked per 15-min interval, paid whether used or not), or a monthly pool (Free, Medium $300, Large $3,000). The per-GB-hour rates come from docs-v1; the pool tiers come from the homepage.
Billing follows the memory tier: 4 vCPU needs the 16 GB tier ($0.96/h on-demand, $0.192/h reserved). Largest sandbox: 16 GB / 4 vCPU (elasticity.md).
Pro ($20) and Max ($200) now buy work minutes for the @Computer coding agent (2,000 and 25,000 minutes, then $0.01/min). They are not sandbox credit, so they are listed under extras, not as plans.
The 4x burst model and peak-rate billing are no longer documented. Autoscale between tiers is opt-in and off by default.

Disk: 20 GB workspace; up to 256 GB on request (closed beta), billed per second at an unpublished rate comparable to EBS gp3. Egress, IPv4 and on-demand concurrency are unpublished. Pool tiers publish concurrency: 5, 50 and 500.
Burst Sandboxes (alpha, about 2x cheaper, processes may restart) have no exact rate, so they are not modeled.
Isolation: QEMU on KVM per the vendor's own guide.

Regions: Serverless Agents take a region setting (us, eu, ap and narrower ones such as eu-north, uk, jp, au); the default is usually the US and account data is not moved. No region setting is documented for bare sandboxes.
Benchmarks: DAX never succeeded; latest burst run failed (2026-09-25).

SSH: no SSH server documented. Interactive access is a PTY "like SSH but over WebSocket" via the SDK. Desktop: install Xvfb, x11vnc and noVNC in the sandbox (documented recipe in the browser-automation guide).
Fork: checkpoints let you "Fork new sandboxes from it ... like git branches for VMs" (disk-only or full disk+memory+CPU checkpoint; warm restore is best effort).
Doc sets are split: docs.opencomputer.dev covers Serverless Agents; the sandbox docs and per-GB-hour rates live on docs-v1.opencomputer.dev.
Idle default: docs disagree (overview: rolling 300 s idle timeout; timeout page: 0 = never auto-hibernate). Set a timeout explicitly.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots the VM state (memory + disk) and stops the VM — no compute cost while hibernated.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: idle timeout expiry (rolling, resets on any exec/file/agent activity); memory + disk included; any SDK call auto-wakes it ('Any operation from the SDK automatically wakes a hibernated sandbox', sub-second restore) and so does a visit to its URL (see wake_on_request). Only when a timeout is set: bare SDK sandboxes default to timeout 0 = never auto-hibernate (troubleshooting page says 300 s; docs inconsistent). Managed agent sessions also 'hibernate when idle, resume where they left off' (homepage).

wake_on_request.quote: When a deployed sandbox receives no traffic, it is automatically hibernated to save resources. When someone visits the deploy URL, the sandbox is woken up on demand.
wake_on_request.note: Stated in the v1 deploy guide only; the preview-URL reference does not say a valid request wakes a sandbox, but implies it ('a brute-force run also can't wake a hibernated sandbox'; 'bad tokens can't burn wake capacity'). The timeout page still suggests calling sandbox.wake() 'to pre-warm a sandbox before routing user traffic to it', so expect wake latency on the first request. Requires a non-zero idle timeout (bare SDK default 0 = never hibernates).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A checkpoint is a named snapshot of a running sandbox. Fork new sandboxes from it to start from a known-good environment — like git branches for VMs.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Full checkpoint (default) = 'Disk, memory, and CPU state'; kind 'disk_only' = rootfs + workspace disk. Restore in place or Sandbox.createFromCheckpoint() to fork many new sandboxes. Also explicit hibernate API and named template Snapshots (image builds). Current sandboxes page: 'checkpoint · fork'.

harness_api.quote: """Agent session API for running Claude Agent SDK inside a sandbox."""
harness_api.note: sandbox.agent.start({prompt, model, systemPrompt, allowedTools, permissionMode, maxTurns, mcpServers, resume}) streams typed events (assistant/result/tool_use_summary/turn_complete), sendPrompt() follow-ups, interrupt(), attach(sessionId), list(). Harness: Claude Agent SDK only; marked @deprecated in the TS SDK in favour of the provider's own Managed/Serverless Agents Management API (https://docs.opencomputer.dev/agents/api: 'Create sessions, send turns, read the event log and manage projects over HTTP'), which runs OpenComputer's own agent loop on an agent computer (models via managed inference, BYOK or a Codex subscription).

egress_allowlist.quote: Requests to hosts not on the list are blocked by the proxy.
egress_allowlist.note: Allowlist is set on a SecretStore attached at sandbox create (exact hosts + wildcards like *.openai.com; empty = all hosts). Enforced by the host-side MITM proxy (outside the VM). Docs inconsistent on the default: how-it-works says 'full outbound internet access via a TAP device with NAT. No firewall or allowlist to configure', while the browser guide says a sandbox without a secretStore 'has no outbound egress at all' (407 from the proxy). No IP/CIDR rules documented; non-HTTP traffic handling undocumented.

egress_http_rules.quote: OpenComputer checks the declared origin, path prefix, method, agent, and environment before sending the outbound request
egress_http_rules.note: Only for the managed Serverless Agents product: defineConnection({origin, methods, pathPrefix, headers}) restricts secret-backed requests by method and path prefix; logged as egress.request/response events. Bare v1 sandboxes: host allowlist + per-secret allowedHosts only (no method/path rules documented).

ingress_rules.quote: To require a bearer token in front of every request, opt in at create time with `previewAuth`.
ingress_rules.note: Preview URLs (sb-<id>-p<port>.workers.opencomputer.dev) are public by default; optional per-sandbox bearer token (Authorization or X-OC-Preview-Token), checked at the control plane before traffic reaches or wakes the VM; token rotatable. One token gates every port. No IP allowlists documented; no public IPv4.

guest_firewall.note: Full Linux VM per sandbox (QEMU/KVM; Firecracker backend also in source) with its own kernel and TAP NIC; docs examples write to /root. Not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: only revealed by a host-side proxy on outbound HTTPS requests
secret_proxy.note: SecretStore secrets are injected into the VM as sealed tokens (osb_sealed_...); the host-side MITM proxy swaps them for the real value on outbound HTTPS to allowed hosts; per-secret allowedHosts. Any HTTP API, not just model keys. HTTPS only; DB/SSH/git not covered (mount credentials for S3/SFTP etc. live in VM tmpfs). Managed agents: secrets 'injected after the request leaves the machine' via declared connections; GitHub App connection hands the agent a short-lived installation token directly.

volume_attach.quote: Mount remote filesystems directly into your sandbox so your code reads and
volume_attach.how: mount your own S3, GCS, Azure Blob, SFTP or WebDAV storage with the Mounts API (rclone FUSE, preview)
volume_attach.note: No provider-hosted attachable volume. The root disk is 20 GB, up to 256 GB on request (closed beta).

volume_shared.quote: Mount remote filesystems directly into your sandbox so your code reads and
volume_shared.note: Preview Mounts API (sandbox.mounts.add) runs rclone FUSE mounts of your own S3/GCS/Azure Blob/SFTP/WebDAV/Dropbox remote; read-write; the same bucket can be mounted by many sandboxes at once (no provider-hosted shared FS; no cross-mount consistency guarantees). Credentials live in VM tmpfs, not via the secret proxy.

docker_inside.quote: Not a container. Real VM with its own kernel, memory, and disk. Hardware-level isolation via KVM.
docker_inside.note: Not explicitly documented for customer workloads (docs only show `sudo docker run ...` for OpenComputer's own self-hosted control-plane host, not inside a customer sandbox). Derived: each sandbox is a full Linux VM with its own kernel and root/sudo access (guides use `sudo apt-get install ...`), so a standard Docker Engine install should run like on any Linux box; not vendor-confirmed for guest use.

nested_virt.quote: Not a container. Real VM with its own kernel, memory, and disk. Hardware-level isolation via KVM.
nested_virt.note: Not documented either way for customer sandboxes: KVM content in the docs describes OpenComputer's own hosts (self-hosting needs nested KVM on the worker). No /dev/kvm guest capability is stated.

computer_use.quote: OpenComputer sandboxes are full Linux VMs, which means you can run a real Chromium browser inside them the same way you would on a laptop.
computer_use.note: No first-party screenshot/click API for agents. Browser automation runs over CDP/Playwright (browser_control); a VNC desktop is a documented self-setup (see desktop).

captcha_solving.quote: If the site has a good API, use the API. A browser is slower, heavier, and flakier. But when you need it, OpenComputer gives you real VMs — not containers — so you can run full Chromium with no Docker-flavored limitations.
captcha_solving.note: No CAPTCHA-solving service is documented in the browser-automation or Browser Sessions docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: full outbound internet access via a TAP device with NAT
egress_ip_type.note: Sandbox egress is plain datacenter NAT through OpenComputer's own host proxy (also used for secret injection); no residential/mobile/proxy IP product is documented anywhere in the sandbox, browser-sessions, or pricing docs.

fork_running.quote: Checkpoint | Original sandbox Keeps running | Can fork Yes — unlimited new sandboxes
fork_running.note: Checkpointing (needed to fork) explicitly does not stop the source sandbox, unlike hibernation which does; `Sandbox.createFromCheckpoint()` can be called any number of times while the original keeps running.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Full checkpoint | Disk, memory, and CPU state | You want the fastest fork or restore path from an exact running VM state.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Full checkpoints (the default) capture memory + CPU state and forks are created from them, but the same page also cautions: 'the platform attempts warm restore when possible, but may fall back to a cold boot. Don't assume running processes carry over' — so it's best-effort, not a hard guarantee.

own_agent_api.quote: Create sessions, send turns, read the event log and manage projects over HTTP with an API key.
own_agent_api.note: OpenComputer's Serverless Agents Management API creates sessions and drives OpenComputer's own managed agent loop (models via useModel/managed inference or BYOK, tools, MCP servers) on a provider-run computer — this superseded/deprecated the earlier Claude-Agent-SDK-specific harness_api. It's a general task-agent API rather than one scoped only to browser/computer-use, but it is the provider's own agent loop, not a bring-your-own coding harness.

lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK (async), shown alongside the TypeScript SDK in every quickstart/example.

lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/Node SDK; the Serverless Agents product is defined as TypeScript functions run with the OpenComputer CLI/SDK.

static_egress_ip.quote: full outbound internet access via a TAP device with NAT
static_egress_ip.note: No static or dedicated outbound IP is documented; outbound traffic goes through a shared host-side NAT and proxy. Serverless Agents can pick an egress region (agents/regions.md), not a fixed IP.

ssh.quote: A PTY session is a full interactive terminal inside the sandbox — like SSH but over WebSocket.
ssh.note: No SSH server/keys; interactive access is a proprietary PTY-over-WebSocket API (`sandbox.pty.create`) and `oc shell`, explicitly described as an SSH substitute, not SSH itself.

desktop.quote: For workflows where the user needs to log in themselves, you can render the browser to a virtual display and expose it via VNC.
desktop.how: install Xvfb, x11vnc, noVNC and websockify in the sandbox and expose noVNC on a preview URL (documented recipe)

image_oci.quote: Declarative images are cached by content hash ... const image = Image.base().aptInstall(['curl', 'jq']).pipInstall(['requests', 'pandas']).env({ PROJECT_ROOT: '/workspace' }).workdir('/workspace');
image_oci.note: custom_image is true via OpenComputer's own declarative Image-builder DSL (apt/pip/run-command steps layered on their base template) and named Snapshots, not by pulling an arbitrary Docker/OCI image; no registry-pull or 'FROM <image>' mechanism found anywhere in the sandbox docs.

public_ipv4.quote: A preview URL is a public HTTPS endpoint that routes traffic to a port inside your sandbox. ... Every sandbox has a built-in `domain` property that gives you instant access to port 80 without creating a preview URL explicitly
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is exclusively via HTTPS reverse-proxy preview URLs (sb-<id>-p<port>.workers.opencomputer.dev); no public IPv4/raw-TCP address is assigned to sandboxes anywhere in the docs.

agent_harnesses.quote: Your Claude Code and Codex, running in our cloud. Mention @Computer in Slack, or call them from your code with the API.
agent_harnesses.how: use the @Computer product (Slack or API), which runs Claude Code and Codex on OpenComputer; billed per work minute, separate from sandbox pricing
agent_harnesses.note: Not preinstalled as CLIs in bare SDK sandboxes. OpenComputer also runs its own managed agent loop (Serverless Agents).

gpu.quote: Free: shared upto 2vCPU, shared upto 2GB memory, 3GB disk, 5 concurrency
gpu.note: No GPU size, type or price on the homepage tiers or in the sandbox docs (CPU-only QEMU/KVM VMs).

windows.quote: A sandbox is a full Linux virtual machine in the cloud.
windows.note: Sandboxes are explicitly defined as Linux VMs only; no Windows machine option exists anywhere in the docs, marketing pages, or SDK reference.

macos.quote: A sandbox is a full Linux virtual machine in the cloud.
macos.note: Product is QEMU/KVM Linux virtualization on Linux hosts; no macOS guest offering exists (macOS only appears as a host platform for the `oc` CLI download, not as a sandbox OS).

arm64.note: Sandboxes run as x86_64 QEMU/KVM guests; the only 'arm64' hits in the docs are the `oc` CLI's own darwin-arm64/linux-arm64 download binaries for the operator's host machine, not a sandbox VM architecture option. No ARM guest sizes/pricing published anywhere.

soc2.quote: ENTERPRISE Custom On your terms Your own cloud or VPC, self-hosted connections Volume pricing and higher limits SSO, audit log, priority support Talk to us
soc2.note: No SOC 2 attestation is documented on the homepage or in either doc set (checked 2026-11-08; the homepage tiers no longer list SSO or audit log either).

hipaa.quote: ENTERPRISE Custom On your terms Your own cloud or VPC, self-hosted connections Volume pricing and higher limits SSO, audit log, priority support Talk to us
hipaa.note: No HIPAA or BAA mention on the homepage or in either doc set.

cpu_class.note: The 4x burst size table is gone from opencomputer.dev/sandboxes. Tiers now map memory to vCPU (1 GB = 1 best-effort, 4 GB = 1, 8 GB = 2, 16 GB = 4). Whether vCPUs are shared or dedicated is not published.

usage_api.quote: GET /api/sandboxes/:id/usage returns a per-minute time series of a sandbox's memory — both the tier you provisioned and what the process actually consumed — together with envelope totals. For cross-sandbox leaderboards (rank by usage, group by tag) see the aggregator at GET /api/usage instead.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: no; REST API + TypeScript SDK return memory allocated/used in GiB-seconds and disk overage in GiB-seconds; these are billable quantities but not costs. Supports per-sandbox usage and groupBy=tag for tag-based aggregation. Documentation states the billing pipeline uses these numbers directly.

custom_domain.quote: Pass a `domain` when creating a preview URL. SSL is provisioned automatically via Cloudflare.
custom_domain.note: Domain verification is set at the organization level in the dashboard.

locations_quote: By default, an agent's sandbox runs wherever capacity is available, usually in the United States.
locations_note: Region choice (us, eu, ap and narrower ones) is documented for Serverless Agents only; account-level data is not moved. No region setting is documented for bare sandboxes.
